title: Migrate Gemini to Interactions API (stateful)
description:
Route all Gemini chat traffic through the Interactions API (`POST /v1beta/interactions`) using `@ai-sdk/google`'s `google.interactions(...)` factory. The previous `:generateContent` path is removed. Stateful mode (`store: true` + `previousInteractionId` chaining) lets the server retain context — after the first turn, only the delta is sent.

## What changed

### Eligibility & discovery

- **Explicit enumerated allowlist** in `getGeminiInteractionsProfile()`. Only models with a profile are surfaced — everything else is excluded (fail-closed). Currently: `gemini-2.5-{pro,flash,flash-lite}`, `gemini-3-flash-preview`, `gemini-3.1-{pro-preview,flash-lite-preview}`, `gemini-3.5-flash`.
- Discovery (`parseResponse`) and `GEMINI_FALLBACK` both filter through `isInteractionsEligible()`.

### Thinking profiles

Thinking levels now match the Interactions API docs per model, not the old budget-based `:generateContent` semantics:

| Model | thinkingLevels | Notes |
|-------|---------------|-------|
| 2.5 Pro | low, medium, high | Cannot disable |
| 2.5 Flash | low, medium, high | Cannot disable; no `minimal` on Interactions API |
| 2.5 Flash-Lite | low, medium, high | Same |
| 3.x Flash-class | minimal, low, medium, high | `minimal` only documented for 3.x |
| 3.x Pro | low, medium, high | Cannot disable |

`"off"` is not in any model's `thinkingEffortLevels` — the Interactions API has no wire-level disable mechanism for default-on models (omitting `thinkingLevel` uses the model default, which is thinking ON).

### Options builder (`buildInteractionsOptions`)

Replaces `geminiThinkingConfig`. Builds `providerOptions.google` with:
- `store: true` (always)
- `previousInteractionId` (when chaining)
- `thinkingLevel` validated against the per-model profile (invalid levels clamped to `"medium"`)
- `thinkingSummaries: "auto"` when the profile supports it

### GeminiClient rewrite

- Always uses `provider.interactions(modelId)`.
- **Stateful chaining**: `extractPreviousInteractionId()` walks backwards through the message array for the most recent `google.interactionId` (checking both message-level and part-level metadata). When found, sends only the delta (messages after the linked assistant response) + `previousInteractionId`.
- **Compaction-aware**: a message marked with `positai.isCompactionSummary` (set by Core) acts as a hard boundary — the helper returns "no prior id", forcing a fresh interaction on the first post-compaction request. Subsequent tool-loop iterations chain normally from the fresh response.
- **Signature filter** (`filterUnsignedReasoning`): drops reasoning parts lacking `google.signature` from initial-interaction history (no `previousInteractionId`). Tool-call parts are retained.
- **Expired-ID recovery**: single retry classified via `APICallError` — requires `statusCode` 400/404 AND the word "interaction" in the error message (not broad `INVALID_ARGUMENT`). Retries with full filtered history, no `previousInteractionId`. No partial first-attempt output (error surfaces at stream start).

### Dependency

`@ai-sdk/google` floor raised from `^3.0.20` → `^3.0.82` (required for `provider.interactions()` support).

## Not in this PR

- Mocked-fetch contract test (verifying `/interactions` URL and request body shape)
- Recovery integration test (stream-level error injection)
- Live smoke test
- Google Search grounding, image output, agents

title: Show summarized thinking from newer Claude models
description:
Reasoning from newer Claude models (Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Fable 5) wasn't appearing as `<thinking>` in the UI, even though the conversation clearly used thinking. The reasoning was present in `lm-messages.jsonl` (persisted with a signature) but absent from `ui-messages.jsonl`.

### Root cause

On Opus 4.7+/Fable 5, the Anthropic API's `thinking.display` defaults to `"omitted"` (a silent change from Opus 4.6, where it was `"summarized"`). With `"omitted"`, thinking blocks stream with **only a signature and empty text**. The accumulator renders `<thinking>` only when there's actual reasoning text, so empty-text blocks get persisted (for the signature) but never shown.

This tracked the model version exactly — across stored conversations, reasoning-blocks-with-text were 99–100% on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 but ~1% on Opus 4.8.

### Changes

- **Send `display: "summarized"`** in the Anthropic provider options for `AnthropicClient`, `SnowflakeClient`, `GoogleVertexClient`, and `BedrockClient`.
- **`PositAiClient` is intentionally excluded** — the Posit AI gateway whitelists thinking properties and rejects `display` with `HTTP 400 ("unexpected additional properties ['display']")`. It stays on `{ type: "adaptive" }` with a comment; re-add `display` once the gateway allows it. (Until then, Claude thinking via Posit AI on Opus 4.7+ remains empty-text.)
- **Bumped `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` (→ ^4.0.113) and `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` (→ ^4.0.142).** They pinned exact older `@ai-sdk/anthropic` copies (3.0.47 / 3.0.58) that predate `display` and would silently strip it. The bump lets all `@ai-sdk/anthropic` copies dedupe to a single 3.0.84.

### Notes

- This only affects the visible reasoning **summary** — thinking happens and is billed identically regardless; the raw chain of thought is never returned by any model.
- Verified the SDK forwards `display` into the request body, the bridge type-checks/builds, and the anthropic copies dedupe to 3.0.84.

title: Increase default max tokens for various Claude models
description:
The default output limits for Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, and Haiku 4.5, were left at the default 16k tokens. This increases the default values to the max for those models.

It also increases the fallback output limit (for models that are not known) from 16k to 64k, so that if any new models come out that this package doesn't know about, they'll get the larger 64k limit.

title: Add `LocalProviderManager.recheckEnabled`
description:
This change adds `LocalProviderManager.recheckEnabled()` and mirrors it in the external-build stub.

# Why

Consumers can already react to local-provider endpoint changes via `onDidChange()`, but there was no way to trigger the same change cascade when the local-provider feature gate changes through a path that `watchEnabled()` does not observe.

In Positron, `experimentalFeatures` can now come from the interleaved `settings.json` config path, not just raw VS Code settings. That means the local-provider gate can flip without the manager's existing `watchEnabled()` listener firing. `recheckEnabled()` gives consumers a narrow, explicit way to say "the gate may have changed; re-emit the local-provider change event" so downstream model/auth/UI refresh logic stays in sync.

# What changed

- Added `LocalProviderManager.recheckEnabled()` in `src/local-providers.ts`
- Added the matching no-op method in `src/local-providers-external.ts`
- Kept the public API surface aligned between full and external variants

# Behavior

`recheckEnabled()` does not recompute endpoint state or mutate cached configuration. It simply re-fires the existing local-provider change event for all local provider IDs so consumers can re-run their normal refresh path.

# Consumer impact

This is a backward-compatible API addition. Existing consumers are unaffected; consumers that need to handle out-of-band gate changes can opt into calling `recheckEnabled()`.

title: Remove unused `conversationId` request-metadata field
description:
This supports posit-dev/assistant#1563. The `chat()` request metadata carried two fields, `{ sessionId?, conversationId? }`, but `conversationId` was **never populated by any consumer** — the agent loop only ever sets `metadata.sessionId` (it carries the conversation ID under `sessionId`). This drops the redundant field and consolidates on the single `sessionId` contract.

### What changed

- **`ModelClient` contract + all client implementations** — removed `conversationId?: string` from the `metadata` object in `ModelClient.ts` and every client (`AnthropicClient`, `BedrockClient`, `CopilotSdkClient`, `DeepSeekClient`, `GeminiClient`, `GoogleVertexClient`, `LMStudioClient`, `OllamaClient`, `OpenAIClient`, `OpenRouterClient`, `PositAiClient`, `SnowflakeClient`, `VscodeLmClient`).
- **`CopilotSdkClient.conversationKeyFor`** was the only reader. It derived the per-conversation routing key for `driversByConversation` (used to resume a Copilot CLI session on tool-result follow-ups) as `conversationId ?? sessionId ?? "__default__"`. Since `conversationId` was always `undefined`, the effective key was always `sessionId ?? "__default__"`. Simplified to exactly that. Also fixed a stale code comment that referenced a non-existent `packages/core/src/request-loop/request-loop.ts` (the mapping lives in `agent-loop.ts`).

### Why it's safe

Behavior-preserving. No producer ever set `conversationId`, so:

- Copilot session routing already keyed on `sessionId` in practice — unchanged.
- `PositAiClient`'s `Session-Id` header (set from `sessionId`) is unaffected.

### Tests

- Added `src/__tests__/conversation-key-for.test.ts` — regression test asserting `conversationKeyFor` derives the routing key from `sessionId` (and falls back to the default key when metadata is absent).

title: Extract pure shapeCredentials into a vscode-free ./credential-shaping entry
description:
## What

Splits the pure half of credential resolution out of `getMappedCredentials` into a new `src/positron/credential-shaping.ts`, shipped as a standalone `./credential-shaping` package export:

- `shapeCredentials(providerId, mapping, rawToken, config)` turns an already-resolved auth token plus a `CredentialConfig` (caller-supplied settings reads) into `ProviderCredentials`: oauth pass-through, google-cloud JSON parsing with ADC fallback, aws JSON parsing with `us-east-1` region default, and apikey baseUrl/customHeaders resolution including the Snowflake URL construction.
- `CONFIG_KEY_OVERRIDES` moves here and is exported.
- `getMappedCredentials` keeps the `vscode.authentication` session lookup and delegates shaping through a vscode/env-backed adapter.

## Why

Positron's headless language-model service (posit-dev/positron#13730 follow-on) needs the shaping logic renderer-side, where the bridge's resolver can't load (vscode-bound + AI-SDK deps). Until now the renderer hand-mirrored ~150 lines of it plus a verbatim `CONFIG_KEY_OVERRIDES` copy, kept in sync by comment. This gives that logic a single owner; Positron consumes the new entry directly.

Why the bridge owns this rather than the auth layer: shaping is provider knowledge, not auth knowledge. Auth deliberately stays generic -- it brokers a session and returns an opaque token. What the shaper knows is per-provider: which JSON fields each brokered token carries (AWS keys, Vertex project/location), the region default, the Snowflake URL construction, and which `authentication.<configKey>.*` namespace each provider reads -- all targeting `ProviderCredentials`, the bridge's own type that provider clients consume. Housing it in an auth layer would point the dependency the wrong way, and the bridge is the only package both consumers (the assistant extension and Positron core) can import.

## Behavior

Unchanged for existing callers: `auth.test.ts` passes untouched, and the delegation adapter preserves the env-folding the vscode path had. The new module's runtime graph carries no `vscode`, AI-SDK, or Node-builtin dependency -- guarded by a test ("has exactly one runtime import: the pure URL helper") so it stays safe to bundle into a browser/renderer.

## Tests

193 lines of new tests on the pure shaper (per-credential-type shaping, malformed-token degradation, region defaulting, Snowflake URL forms, purity guard). Full suite: 8 files / 127 tests passing; format, lint, and type checks clean.

title: Add registerAllProviders orchestrator
description:
This PR is an attempt to deepen the module that is the ai-provider-bridge. Before, when a consumer used the provider bridge it still needed to import all the providers and declare them in the code etc which meant a lot of leaky abstractions and made updating and adding a new provider more complicated than simply bumping the version of this package. 

The two areas that really need to actually be paid attention to are the two different`registerAllProviders` functions. These recreate what the consumers previously were doing, but in the case of ones that want all of the dependencies, it provides them with all of it without needing to do anything more. 

I verified by building a tarball locally and then updating the Positron headless LM PR to verify it works as expected.

_Agent generated notes below  👇_

## Summary

Deepens `ai-provider-bridge` so a consumer uses it through a tiny surface -- one dependency and one registration call -- instead of importing and wiring every provider itself. Two coordinated changes:

1. **`registerAllProviders` orchestrator** -- centralizes the "register every provider into a `ProviderRegistry`" loop consumers were hand-rolling, with internal + external build variants that keep external/OSS bundles free of the 14 provider SDKs.
2. **The bridge owns its provider SDKs** -- the provider SDKs move from `peerDependencies` to `dependencies`, and the `ai` types in the public API are re-exported, so a consumer's `package.json` collapses to a single `ai-provider-bridge` line.

## 1. registerAllProviders orchestrator

- **Orchestrator** (`register-all-providers.ts`): `registerAllProviders(registry, logger, config)` iterates an exported `PROVIDER_REGISTRARS` table (`[ProviderId, (registry, logger, config) => void]`), honoring `config.allowedProviders`. The caller owns the registry lifecycle. Exposed on both provider barrels.
- **External variant** (`register-all-providers-external.ts`): same signature, registers positai only. Imports only positai plus the shared contract leaf -- it does not reference `register-all-providers.ts` at all, so no non-positai SDK can enter the external bundle.
- **Shared contract leaf** (`provider-registration.ts`): holds the `ProviderRegistrationConfig` interface, the `RegisterAllProviders` signature type, and the `isProviderAllowed` predicate -- the single definition both variants share. Everything but the one-line predicate is type-only (erased at build), so the leaf adds no runtime/SDK code to the external bundle.

### Hardening (comment-enforced invariants -> structural guarantees)

- **Signature-parity pin**: both `registerAllProviders` variants are annotated with a shared `RegisterAllProviders` function type (defined once in `provider-registration.ts`). Arity/return drift between the internal and external builds is a compile error rather than relying on SYNC NOTE comments.
- **Structural bundle split**: the external variant no longer imports `register-all-providers.ts` at all (shared types live in the leaf), so SDK leakage into the lightweight bundle is impossible by construction -- no guard test needed.
- **Id-coverage test**: asserts the `PROVIDER_REGISTRARS` ids equal `PROVIDER_IDS` by name, not just count, so a mislabeled / duplicate / missing id fails a test.
- **Empty allow-list test** in both variants (`allowedProviders: []` registers nothing).

## 2. Consumers depend only on `ai-provider-bridge`

Before, a consumer (e.g. Positron's headless LM engine) had to declare every provider SDK in its own `package.json` (they were optional `peerDependencies`) and import `ai` directly for `ModelMessage`. Now the bridge owns it:

- All provider SDKs are regular `dependencies` (still `external` at build time -- resolved from `node_modules`, not inlined, since `@aws-sdk/*` / `google-auth-library` bundle poorly).
- `ModelMessage` and `LanguageModelUsage` are re-exported from the root entrypoint, so consumers build chat requests (`ModelMessage`) and implement custom `StepLogger`s (`LanguageModelUsage` on `StepLogData.usage`) without importing `ai`.
- `vscode` remains the one optional peer (host-provided; only `/positron` imports it).

Result: a consumer declares just `"ai-provider-bridge"`.

**Trade-off:** an external / positai-only build now *installs* all the SDKs even though its *bundle* references only the Posit AI ones (the bundle stays slim via the `-external` aliasing). That is the deliberate cost of single-dependency consumption; if slim external installs ever matter, the lever is tiering the non-positai SDKs into `optionalDependencies` + `npm install --omit=optional`.

## Testing

- `npm run check-types`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (114 tests), and `npm run build` all green.
- `package-lock.json` regenerated; SDKs verified under root `dependencies`, `peerDependencies` reduced to `vscode`.
- Built `dist/` verified: `ModelMessage` and `LanguageModelUsage` re-exported from the root, internal bundle still externalizes the SDKs (not inlined), external bundle graph reaches only positai deps.

## Release note

No version bump in this branch -- releases are tag-driven. Cut `v0.0.9` on `main` after merge, per the Releasing section of `CLAUDE.md`. On that bump, consumers can adopt `registerAllProviders` and drop their provider-SDK lines in one step.

title: fix base url normalization for several providers
description:
- fixes #3 
- addresses https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/13976, but I'll need to get this into Posit Assistant first and release the extension

## changes

Add a shared `normalizeProviderBaseUrl(baseUrl, host, version)` helper in `src/utils.ts` and wire it into the Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini providers (both the model-list fetch and the chat client). It:

- Falls back to the versioned default (`host/version`) when the base URL is undefined, empty, or whitespace-only.
- Appends the version segment when the value is exactly the known host with no path (e.g. `https://api.anthropic.com` -> `https://api.anthropic.com/v1`).
- Leaves any other host untouched, so custom proxies/gateways that legitimately route without a version segment keep working.
- Strips trailing slashes.

DeepSeek and the OpenAI-compatible provider keep their no-`/v1` behaviour (their SDKs accept the host without version), but now also trim whitespace-only base URLs.

## testing

Confirm Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini work end to end in Posit Assistant when the bridge is the one resolving the base URL, i.e. either:

- `assistant.modelRouting` is set to **direct**, or
- `positron.assistant.enable` is **false**

For each of the three providers:

1. Configure the provider with a valid API key and **leave the base URL blank**. Models should list and chat should work (default host + version path).
2. Set the base URL to the **bare host** with no version segment (`https://api.anthropic.com`, `https://api.openai.com`, `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`). Models should still list and chat should still work.
3. Set the base URL to the host **with** the version segment (`.../v1`, `.../v1beta`). Behaviour should be unchanged from step 2.
